query: The Board believes HRMP is obligated to complete the Taste of Queens food hall.

facts.text: The Board expressed a belief that HRMP should complete Taste of Queens.
The Board states the food hall was outside HRMP's commitments in its application.
The Board's chart nevertheless includes $60 million for Taste of Queens buildout.
HRMP described its role as delivering the parking podium for the food hall.
A Mets-affiliated entity was expected to build the Taste of Queens food hall.
The proposed food hall was roughly 30,000 square feet.
The license incorporates application and CAC commitments generally without expressly naming the food hall.
Press coverage attributed a June 1, 2030 target for food hall completion to Commission filings.

reference_verdict.reasoning: The sentence is the Board's belief, not a finding, a recommended license condition or an HRMP undertaking. The license does not name the food hall; it binds only through the general CAC-commitments clause, and the Commission has not said whether that covers it. The builder is the Mets entity; HRMP's part is the podium. Delivery is scheduled for 2030, so if the CAC-clause reading is adopted the status would be 'not yet due'.

sources.title: GFLB Selection document (1 Dec 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: pdf p.20: "the Board strongly believes that HRMP has an obligation to complete the food hall." Also: the food hall "was not part of HRMP's commitments in its application" and is "being built by the New York Mets" on a ~$60M garage overbuild.
sources.notes: Quote verified verbatim against project source text (char 44895-44977).

sources.title: GFLB Report and Findings (Mar 2026)
sources.specific_evidence: Same sentence (printed pp.30-31). Chart 5 counts "Taste of Queens Buildout $60" million inside the $761M community benefits, although the text says the hall was not considered.
sources.notes: Internal tension: excluded from deliberations but counted in the benefits total.

sources.title: HRMP responses to CAC inquiries (29 Sep 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: "HRMP will unlock further development potential ... by delivering a parking podium on which Queens Baseball Company (i.e., the New York Mets) will then build the Taste of Queens." ~30,000 sq ft, ~20 local vendors.
sources.notes: HRMP's own undertaking is the podium; the Mets entity builds the hall.

sources.title: HRMP application: Local Impact Siting, Local Business (Jun 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: HRMP "understands that an entity affiliated with the New York Mets expects to build Taste of Queens."

sources.title: HRMP license award and Exhibit 1 License Conditions (19 Dec 2025; effective 15 Dec 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: Does not name this item. Exhibit 1: "Hard Rock shall materially perform consistent with the content of its Application and commitments expressed during the Community Advisory Committee evaluative process, as determined or otherwise approved by the Commission."
sources.notes: Food hall, overbuild and Mets not mentioned. CAC clause is the only plausible binding route.

sources.title: Gaming Commission public meeting transcript (15 Dec 2025)
sources.specific_evidence: Food hall not discussed. Only stated condition: an independent monitor for at least 5 years.

sources.title: Queens Daily Eagle, 'Metropolitan Park casino construction running months behind schedule' (15 May 2026)
sources.specific_evidence: Commission filings say "the construction of the casino, a food hall, open space areas, and improvements to the Mets-Willets Point 7 train station will conclude by June 1, 2030"; project ~5.5 months behind.
